text:
lia: heads up — CI perf alarm popped on the kv-cache memory budget tests after yesterday's kernel-router merge (PR#2753). several long-ctx tests hit OOMs in the smoke matrix. filing here so we don't roll forward.

michael: copying logs? which tests failed?

lia: short log snippet: 
```
2026-03-18T14:12:03Z test: kv_memory_budget.smoke.longctx_16k: OOM after 4.2s
pmap: total 24.1G, rss 22.9G
stack: kv-slab growth spike at alloc hotpath
```

sophia: repro steps? can we reproduce locally on a dev GPU?

lia: yes repro is reliable on the perf rig: `./scripts/run_perf_test --profile kv --seq 16384 --batch 8 --iters 20` — it climbs steady until OOM. saving heap profiles to /tmp/kv_profiles/*.heap

raj: I think this lines up with my local run. quick `perf top` showed high spend in `slab_alloc_slowpath` and `kv_compact_scan`. fragmentation ratio goes from ~1.1 -> 2.8 right before OOM.

michael: rollout note: the merged change to kernel routing switched some long-seq traffic to fast-path-v2 kernels (commit 9f4b2a1). that also changed the eviction predicate from age-based LRU to a lightweight frequency bias when `seq_len > 4096`. wondering if combination is causing many small slices to be retained and never coalesced.

lia: attaching the minimal config diff that reproduced locally: 
```
--- a/runtime/router/config.go
+++ b/runtime/router/config.go
@@ -210,7 +210,9 @@ func selectKernel(meta) {
-    if meta.SeqLen > 4096 { return KernelFastV1 }
+    if meta.SeqLen > 4096 {
+        // route to fast v2 for better throughput
+        return KernelFastV2
+    }
 }
```

sophia: can you paste the heap delta from the profiler?

lia: heap profile (delta top 5): 
```
+6.8G  kv_slab_fragmentation
+3.2G  kv_cache_object_meta
+2.1G  kv_prefetch_buffers
+1.0G  misc_alloc
```

raj: that + the perf symbols imply the new kernel path allocs larger alignment (64->256) for the KV entries which increases padding and prevents coalescing in the slab arena. i saw increased internal fragmentation in mmap regions.

michael: ok hypothesis: kernel routing -> fast-v2 -> larger alignment -> fragmentation -> compactor scanning thrash -> memory blowout. can we confirm alignment change? grep commit for align constants.

lia: found it: commit 9f4b2a1 changed `KV_ENTRY_ALIGN` from 64 to 256 under fast-v2 to satisfy avx512 tile load.

sophia: who added that change? iirc it was for throughput on mid-length sequences. might be safe for short-lived sessions but not for long-ctx.

michael: action plan: 1) hold rollout for kernel-router (tagging product/ops), 2) bisect to confirm commit is causal, 3) open revert or feature-flag the alignment change behind `kv_align_opt` and default to 64 for seq>4096 workloads.

lia: started quick bisect: reverting 9f4b2a1 locally fixes the OOM repro (ran same script: memory stable ~8G rss).

raj: nice. also ran `kv-compact --diagnose` and it shows compaction CPU burning up when alignment=256. attach snippet: 
```
compactor: scanned 48 slabs, reclaimed 0 bytes, cpu 120s
```

michael: please open a revert PR and add a test for a long-ctx perf smoke to CI. tag me + eng-sre. this is a rollout blocker for the router change.

lia: filed PR 2762 to revert the align bump and added `kv_longctx_perf` smoke test to `ci/perf/smoke.yml`. forcing hold on the original rollout: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2762

sophia: +1 on revert. long-ctx is a tier-1 workload for Dedicated customers. we should also consider adding a runtime flag so teams can opt-in to the AVX alignment on controlled fleets.

raj: will follow up with a proposal to add an alignment-aware arena that avoids cross-slab padding — low-risk but longer term.

michael: sounds good. posting incident note and setting rollout to blocked. lia can you patch the release notes and add the perf graphs to the PR?

lia: on it — attaching before/after memory graphs and flamegraph. i'll merge revert once CI green. tagging @eng-sre for follow-up on canary policy. :lock: :warning:

eng-bot: Deploy hold set on rollout 'kernel-router-v2' by michael — reason: kv cache OOM regression on long-ctx perf smoke.

michael: thanks. we should do a short postmortem after revert with root cause summary + mitigation (test + flag + longer-term allocator work).
